title: README
universal_lens: The sovereign primitives form a unified operator algebra over the Hilbert space of NFL plays. Aggressiveness acts as a coverage-density weighting, DAKOTA/YBC represent expectation-adjusted efficiency kernels, and TPRR serves as a conditional probability functional mapping defensive state vectors to offensive yield distributions.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats these primitives as latent variables in a hierarchical Bayesian model. Conformal prediction intervals are constructed around DAKOTA and YBC using historical residuals, while TPRR provides covariate shifts for dynamic calibration against varying defensive look priors.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes these operators within a Markov Decision Process (MDP). The state-transition matrix is modulated by Aggressiveness and TPRR, calculating optimal action-value functions (Q-values) that maximize expected EPA/Play under specific defensive constraints and play-action conditions.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Author definition: "DAKOTA is an all-in-one quarterback efficiency score that measures how well a passer runs their offense compared to expectations." Chart-branded "DYNATYZE NFL · THE TAPE".
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D \in \mathbb{R} representing the residual difference between realized EPA/Play and context-adjusted expected EPA/Play.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the underlying expectation model perfectly accounts for situational variables (down, distance, field position, personnel).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in extreme outlier regimes (e.g., garbage time, prevent defense) where the baseline expectation model suffers from sparse training data.

layer2.telemetry: Empirical observable: Dynatyze proprietary DAKOTA score.

primitives.name: Pre-Contact Yield Vector
primitives.verbatim_quote: Author definition: "Yards Before Contact shows the total yards before a player is first touched." Footer: "Every row clears 9+ opp.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Y_{bc} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} measured in yards, denoting spatial displacement prior to the first defensive collision event.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes tracking data can precisely isolate the exact coordinate and timestamp of the first physical contact.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation of these sovereign primitives begins by abstracting raw sports analytics into fundamental mathematical operators acting upon the state space of an NFL game. We define the primary state vector S_t at any given play t, encompassing down, distance, field position, and personnel. The `qb_aggressiveness_density` primitive operates as a scalar multiplier on the transition probability matrix P(S_{t+1}|S_t, A), specifically penalizing passing actions A under high defensive density. This aligns with the Next Gen Stats metric, treating tight coverage as a constraint that reduces the effective volume of available passing lanes.

Simultaneously, the `dakota_efficiency_kernel` and `yards_before_contact_vector` serve as dual evaluation functions. DAKOTA measures the divergence between the realized trajectory of the state evolution and the theoretically optimal path predicted by a context-aware baseline model. Mathematically, it is a residual kernel R = Y_{actual} - E[Y|S_t]. Similarly, YBC isolates the initial velocity vector imparted to the ball carrier before the collision manifold is engaged. By separating pre-contact yield from post-contact resistance, we decouple offensive line performance from running back agility.

The duality emerges when combining these operators: Aggressiveness dictates the risk profile of the state transition, while DAKOTA and YBC quantify the efficiency of the execution within that risk profile. Failure modes arise primarily from data sparsity—when N approaches zero in early-season weeks, the expectation models E[Y|S_t] become highly volatile, causing the residual kernels to reflect noise rather than true skill. Furthermore, the discrete nature of 'contact' introduces step-function discontinuities in the YBC operator, requiring smoothing techniques to maintain differentiability for gradient-based optimization in the GSE engine.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: These primitives trace their lineage to mid-20th-century stochastic process theory and modern Expected Points Added (EPA) frameworks. The concept of measuring efficiency relative to expectation (DAKOTA) mirrors the development of alpha metrics in quantitative finance, isolating manager skill from market beta. YBC extends the classical physics decomposition of momentum transfer, applying it to biological collision systems. Aggressiveness draws from information theory, quantifying the entropy reduction caused by defensive spatial constraints.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires viewing the head coach and quarterback as bounded rational actors optimizing these very primitives. A high Aggressiveness score implies the offensive decision-maker perceives a higher utility in high-variance, high-reward state transitions despite defensive pressure. Conversely, a defense deploying a 2-high shell aims to manipulate the offensive agent's perception, forcing them into low-efficiency kernels. The primitives thus capture not just physical outcomes, but the psychological博弈 (game) of exploiting perceived inefficiencies in the opponent's strategy.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity vetoes are critical here. DAKOTA and standard EPA/Play are highly correlated; however, DAKOTA explicitly strips out situational beta, making it orthogonal to raw volume metrics. We must veto any model update where YBC and overall Yards Per Carry (YPC) diverge solely due to small-sample noise in tackle location tracking. Furthermore, Aggressiveness must be cross-checked against Completion Percentage Over Expectation (CPOE); if Aggressiveness rises but CPOE remains stable, it indicates a genuine skill upgrade rather than a schematic shift toward reckless throwing, preventing leakage of schematic noise into the talent evaluation layer.
